title: Internal Hom comparison of a strong monoidal equivalence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with internal Homs: for each $M$, tensoring $M\otimes-$ has a specified right adjoint $[M,-]$, with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}:M\otimes[M,N]\to N$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a strong monoidal functor [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] whose underlying functor is an equivalence. Write $\mu_{M,L}:FM\otimes FL\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M\otimes L)$ for its tensorator. For $M,N\in\mathcal C$, define
$$c_{F;M,N}:F[M,N]\longrightarrow[FM,FN]$$
to be the transpose under the specified tensor/internal-Hom adjunction in $\mathcal D$ of
$$FM\otimes F[M,N]\xrightarrow{\mu_{M,[M,N]}}F(M\otimes[M,N])\xrightarrow{F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})}FN.$$
Then $c_{F;M,N}$ is an isomorphism, natural contravariantly in $M$ and covariantly in $N$. In particular it is the specified evaluation comparison, satisfying
$$\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}\circ(1_{FM}\otimes c_{F;M,N})=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\circ\mu_{M,[M,N]}.$$
No dualizability condition on $M$ is imposed.

proof.text:
Write $\Phi^{\mathcal C}_{M;X,N}$ and $\Phi^{\mathcal D}_{FM;Z,FN}$ for the specified adjunction bijections, from tensor morphisms to internal-Hom morphisms. Their inverse sends $h:X\to[M,N]$ to $\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(1_M\otimes h)$. Thus, putting $a=F[M,N]$, $b=[FM,FN]$, and $c=c_{F;M,N}$, the definition of $c$ gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(1_{FM}\otimes c)=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\mu_{M,[M,N]}.$$
Throughout this proof composition is right to left. This is the required evaluation equation, directly from the inverse adjunction bijection.

proof.text:
For each $X\in\mathcal C$, consider this chain of bijections:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FX,a)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,[M,N])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M\otimes X,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(M\otimes X),FN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FM\otimes FX,FN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FX,b).$$
The first and third use full faithfulness of the underlying equivalence; the second and fifth are the given adjunctions; the fourth is precomposition with the tensorator isomorphism of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. To spell out full faithfulness here, choose $G$ with natural isomorphisms $\eta:1\cong GF$, $\epsilon:FG\cong1$. Faithfulness of $F$ follows by conjugating $GF(f)$ with $\eta$; faithfulness of $G$ follows similarly with $\epsilon$. For $h:FX\to FY$, take $k=\eta_Y^{-1}G(h)\eta_X$; naturality of $\eta$ gives $GF(k)=G(h)$, and faithfulness of $G$ gives $F(k)=h$. This proves the required Hom bijections without an extra categorical theorem.

proof.text:
Every $h:FX\to a$ is uniquely $F(k)$ for $k:X\to[M,N]$. The chain of Step 2 sends it to the transpose of $F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(1_M\otimes k))\mu_{M,X}$. Tensorator naturality in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] and Step 1 give
$$F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(1\otimes k))\mu_{M,X}=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\mu_{M,[M,N]}(1\otimes Fk)=\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(1\otimes cFk).$$
Hence that bijection is precisely $h\mapsto ch$. For every $Z\in\mathcal D$, choose an isomorphism $s:FX\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ using essential surjectivity (one can take $X=GZ$ and $s=\epsilon_Z$). Precomposition with $s$ identifies $h\mapsto ch$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(Z,a)$ with this bijection on $\operatorname{Hom}(FX,a)$. Thus postcomposition with $c$ is bijective for every $Z$.

proof.text: Surjectivity for $Z=b$ supplies $d:b\to a$ with $cd=1_b$. Then $c(dc)=(cd)c=c=c1_a$, so injectivity for $Z=a$ gives $dc=1_a$. This is an explicit two-sided inverse, and proves invertibility without invoking Yoneda or a right-adjoint uniqueness theorem.

proof.text:
For $v:N\to N'$, put $p=[M,v]$, $q=[FM,Fv]$. Naturality in the target of the specified adjunctions says $\operatorname{ev}_{M,N'}(1\otimes p)=v\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN'}(1\otimes q)=Fv\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}$. Therefore Step 1 and tensorator naturality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] give
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN'}(1\otimes c_{F;M,N'}Fp)&=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N'})\mu_{M,[M,N']}(1\otimes Fp)\\
&=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N'}(1\otimes p))\mu_{M,[M,N]}\\
&=Fv\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(1\otimes c_{F;M,N})\\
&=\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN'}(1\otimes q c_{F;M,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $c_{F;M,N'}Fp=q c_{F;M,N}$, the asserted covariant naturality.

proof.text:
For $u:M'\to M$, define $p=[u,N]:[M,N]\to[M',N]$ as the transpose of $\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(u\otimes1)$, and define $q=[Fu,FN]$ by the identical rule in $\mathcal D$. These are the contravariant internal-Hom maps, so by their definition
$$\operatorname{ev}_{M',N}(1\otimes p)=\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(u\otimes1),\qquad \operatorname{ev}_{FM',FN}(1\otimes q)=\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(Fu\otimes1).$$
Step 1 and tensorator naturality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] now give
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ev}_{FM',FN}(1\otimes c_{F;M',N}Fp)&=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M',N}(1\otimes p))\mu_{M',[M,N]}\\
&=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(u\otimes1))\mu_{M',[M,N]}\\
&=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\mu_{M,[M,N]}(Fu\otimes1)\\
&=\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(Fu\otimes c_{F;M,N})\\
&=\operatorname{ev}_{FM',FN}(1\otimes q c_{F;M,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $c_{F;M',N}Fp=q c_{F;M,N}$. This supplies contravariant naturality with no braiding, symmetry, or dualizability hypothesis.
